title: Nia’s Great River Journey
style: warm realistic wildlife storybook photography look, natural African light, anatomically believable animals, gentle child-friendly emotion, cinematic but not frightening
summary: Young elephant Nia travels with her herd along a winding river, meets hippos, kingfishers and buffalo, helps move litter to safety for park rangers, and learns that clean water keeps every living thing alive.

characters.name: Nia
characters.visualDescription: A young African elephant calf with soft dusty-grey skin, large fan-shaped ears edged with pale pink, small white tusks just beginning to show, and a bright green leaf tucked behind her left ear. She walks on four sturdy legs with a short tufted tail.

characters.name: Aunt Amara
characters.visualDescription: A tall adult African elephant with deep grey wrinkled skin, wide ears with grey edges, long curved ivory tusks, and a calm, watchful expression. She walks at the front of the herd, trunk gently curled.

characters.name: Kito
characters.visualDescription: A hippopotamus with a round barrel-shaped body, pinkish-brown skin, short stubby legs, small rounded ears, wide yawning mouth, and short tail. He rests half-submerged in river shallows.

characters.name: Zuri
characters.visualDescription: A malachite kingfisher with a bright blue back, orange chest, small red beak, tiny pink legs, and a short tail. She perches on reeds or low branches beside the river.

characters.name: Grandmother Buffalo
characters.visualDescription: An African buffalo with dark charcoal horns curving down and inward, weathered grey-brown hide, sturdy legs, and a long tufted tail. She stands calmly at the edge of a grassy clearing.

pages.text: Nia the young elephant woke early, her ears pink in the morning sun. Today her herd would follow the great river. She tucked a green leaf behind her ear and trumpeted, "Let's go!"

pages.text: The elephants walked in a gentle line beside the sparkling water. Nia splashed with her trunk, spraying silver drops into the air. Aunt Amara smiled. "The river will show us many friends today," she said.

pages.text: In the shallows, Kito the hippopotamus yawned a wide, bubbly yawn. "Good morning!" he spluttered. "My river is lovely and cool. Would you like a drink?" Nia sipped carefully. The water tasted fresh and sweet.

pages.text: On a swaying reed sat Zuri the kingfisher, bright as a blue jewel. "I fish here every day," she chirped. "Clear water helps me see my supper!" Nia watched her dive, quick as a wink.

pages.text: Farther along, Nia noticed colourful rubbish caught among the reeds. An old sack and empty bottles floated at the water’s edge. "That does not belong in the river," she said.

pages.text: Aunt Amara looked carefully. "Litter can dirty water or trap an animal. We shall lift it onto dry ground, where the park rangers can collect it safely." Nia nodded.

pages.text: Soon the litter rested in a neat pile on dry ground, ready for the rangers. Fish flicked their tails in the clear shallows, while Zuri swooped happily above the water.

pages.text: In a grassy clearing stood Grandmother Buffalo. "Thank you, kind elephants," she rumbled. "My herd drinks downstream. Clean water keeps us all strong." Nia stood tall. She felt proud, helpful, and very, very thirsty!

pages.text: That evening, the herd bathed in the calm, clean river. Nia floated happily, her leaf still tucked behind her ear. "One river," she murmured, "for hippos, kingfishers, buffalo and elephants. Water for everyone." The stars twinkled goodnight.
